fatal_errors: The proposed Fe-0.1C-1Mn conventional steel is not the target AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The hypothesis substitutes mechanical testing temperature for the required intermediate-temperature aging treatment.
The proposed -100°C to 200°C range does not match the approximately 550-750°C aging window.
Grain-boundary segregation and classical temper embrittlement contradict the target phase-boundary and L12-ordering mechanism.
The arbitrary 50% ductility loss at 0°C is unsupported by evidence.
The experiment does not measure high-temperature ductility recovery or distinguish the proposed mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the general idea of a ductile-brittle-ductile response but otherwise addresses a different material, intervention, temperature regime, and mechanism. The target is an as-cast FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA aged near 600°C and 750°C, with embrittlement arising from enhanced L12 ordering and jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries and recovery occurring as ordering decreases and ductile phase-boundary transition zones form. The generated experiment compares only -100°C and 0°C ductility, so it neither demonstrates a complete non-monotonic transition nor tests the decisive microstructural signatures. No supporting evidence is supplied, and its numerical thresholds are arbitrary.
